stem: Cerebrospinal fluid is primarily produced by which of the following structures:
fact: CSF is primarily produced by the choroid plexus in the lateral, third, and fourth ventricles, with most production from the lateral ventricles.
mnemonic: Choroid makes the fluid; granulations drain it.
finding: The ventricular-system reference identifies the choroid plexus as the principal site of CSF production.

stem: The Broca's speech area is located in which of the following regions:
fact: Broca area is in the dominant inferior frontal region and supports expressive language production.
mnemonic: Broca builds speech in the frontal lobe.
finding: The cerebral-cortex reference locates the expressive language region in the dominant frontal lobe.

stem: Which of the following clinical features is most suggestive of a lesion of the temporal lobe:
options: Conjugate eye deviation towards the side of the lesion
fact: Receptive dysphasia points to dysfunction of Wernicke area in the dominant posterior temporal lobe.
mnemonic: Temporal Wernicke receives meaning; frontal Broca produces speech.
finding: The temporal-lobe reference supports the association between posterior temporal language cortex and receptive dysphasia.

stem: Which of the following clinical features would you least expect to see in a lesion of the frontal lobe:
options: Spastic paralysis of the contralateral leg
Contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing
fact: Contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing localizes to the occipital visual cortex rather than the frontal lobe.
mnemonic: Frontal plans and moves; occipital sees.
finding: Cortical motor and executive functions are frontal, whereas primary visual cortex is occipital.

stem: Which of the following is most likely to cause a bitemporal hemianopia:
fact: A pituitary adenoma can compress the optic chiasm and interrupt crossing nasal retinal fibres, causing bitemporal hemianopia.
mnemonic: Pituitary pressure at the chiasm cuts both temporal fields.
finding: Optic-chiasm compression, including from pituitary tumours, produces bitemporal field loss.

stem: Which of the following arteries is the terminal branch of the basilar artery:
fact: The basilar artery terminates by bifurcating into the right and left posterior cerebral arteries.
finding: The posterior-circulation reference identifies the posterior cerebral arteries as terminal branches of the basilar artery.

stem: The extracranial portion of the optic nerve is supplied by which of the following blood vessels:
fact: The ophthalmic artery supplies the optic nerve in its orbital/anterior course.
mnemonic: Ophthalmic artery accompanies the optic nerve into the orbit.
finding: The orbit reference supports the displayed ophthalmic-artery answer; page 1910 is the answer-reviewed duplicate state.

stem: The extracranial portion of the optic nerve is supplied by which of the following blood vessels:
fact: The ophthalmic artery supplies the optic nerve in its orbital/anterior course.
mnemonic: Ophthalmic artery accompanies the optic nerve into the orbit.
finding: The answer-reviewed duplicate displays ophthalmic artery as the correct answer and provides the complete option list.

stem: What type of visual field defect are you likely to see in a lesion of the temporal optic radiation:
fact: A temporal optic-radiation lesion involving Meyer loop causes contralateral homonymous superior quadrantanopia.
mnemonic: Meyer loops low in the temporal lobe, so the upper visual field is lost.
finding: The visual-field reference supports superior quadrantanopia from temporal optic-radiation involvement.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a typical cerebellar sign:
fact: Resting tremor is associated with parkinsonism; cerebellar dysfunction more typically causes intention tremor, dysmetria, ataxia, hypotonia, and dysarthria.
mnemonic: Cerebellar tremor appears with intention, not at rest.
finding: The cerebellum reference distinguishes intention tremor and coordination signs from parkinsonian resting tremor.
